name: Austin
tagline: Live Music, No State Income Tax, and Year-Round Sunshine
description: Austin combines a vibrant cultural scene with zero state income tax, making it a compelling domestic FIRE destination. The city offers world-class dining, outdoor recreation along the Colorado River, and a booming tech economy if you ever want to un-retire. While housing costs have risen sharply, Austin still undercuts coastal cities and rewards careful budgeting with an exceptional quality of life.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.climate: Subtropical with hot summers and mild winters

housing.description: Cheapest acceptable older studio or 1BR in a workable central-adjacent area — East Riverside–Oltorf or the North Loop edge (asking rents have softened citywide)

dining.description: Mostly home cooking; taco trucks and casual eateries a few times a week

healthcare.description: ACA marketplace Silver plan, subsidized if MAGI is kept under the 2026 400%-FPL cliff (~$62,600 single); assumes an early retiree (45–55) — older retirees budget more. Texas has no state backfill and did not expand Medicaid, so above the cliff this line jumps toward the full ~$925/mo sticker.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with insurance and gas — a car is essential (Texas auto insurance runs above the US average)

entertainment.description: Free live music on 6th Street, Barton Springs, parks; an occasional concert ticket

1M.lifestyle: A cheapest-acceptable older studio or one-bedroom in a central-adjacent area like East Riverside — and Austin's steep 2024–2026 rent softening means the Lean housing line lands lower than the city's reputation suggests. A car is essential and summer A/C spikes the electric bill, but Texas's zero state income tax means every dollar of the withdrawal stays put. Free live music on 6th Street and swimming at Barton Springs keep entertainment near-free. The ACA Silver premium stays low only if MAGI is kept under the 2026 ~$62,600 cliff — Texas has no backfill.

housing.description: A decent typical 1BR in a solid neighborhood — South Lamar, North Loop, or East Austin

dining.description: Dining out several times a week at mid-range restaurants; weekend brunch culture

healthcare.description: A Silver plan; net cost low only if MAGI is managed under the ~$62,600 cliff (no Texas backfill)

transportation.description: A reliable car with full coverage for Hill Country weekends

entertainment.description: ACL and SXSW tickets, paddle boarding on Lady Bird Lake, a gym membership

2M.lifestyle: A decent one-bedroom in South Lamar, the North Loop, or East Austin, dining out several times a week at mid-range spots, and live music shows on the regular. A reliable car covers Hill Country weekends, and ACL or SXSW tickets, a gym membership, and paddle boarding on Lady Bird Lake all fit. No state income tax stretches the budget, and coverage is comfortable — an easygoing, culturally rich life.

housing.description: A high-quality 1BR in a walkable district — Travis Heights, Zilker, or a nicer downtown unit

dining.description: Regular dining at top tables like Uchi and Emmer & Rye; daily coffee-shop culture

healthcare.description: A Gold-tier plan; padded near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff where premium tax credits disappear (Texas benchmarks rose ~35% for 2026)

transportation.description: A late-model SUV or sedan, premium insurance, occasional rideshare

entertainment.description: Season tickets, a boat rental on Lake Travis, a premium gym, regular live events

3M.lifestyle: A high-quality place in Travis Heights or Zilker, or a nicer downtown unit, with regular dinners at Uchi and Emmer & Rye and weekend trips to Fredericksburg wine country. A late-model SUV, boat rentals on Lake Travis, and season tickets are all easy, and healthcare is a padded Gold plan near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff. With no state income tax, this is a comfortably affluent Austin life with a real travel budget.

housing.description: A luxury downtown high-rise condo or an upscale rental in a prime district

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining plus occasional private-chef entertaining

healthcare.description: An unsubsidized Gold/Platinum plan plus concierge or direct primary care

transportation.description: A luxury vehicle plus premium insurance and detailing

entertainment.description: VIP festival passes (ACL, F1), a country club membership, lake weekends

domesticHelp.description: Bi-weekly house cleaning, landscaping, occasional personal-assistant tasks

luxuryExtras.description: Quarterly travel, premium wine subscriptions, spa days, philanthropy

5M.lifestyle: A luxury downtown high-rise or an upscale rental in a prime district, a housekeeper, and a nice car, with near-daily dining at the city's best restaurants. VIP passes for ACL and the F1 Grand Prix, a country club membership, and business-class travel are all comfortable. Texas's zero state income tax is a major lever here — this budget goes much further in Austin than the same money would in California or New York.

housing.description: A top-of-market estate or penthouse — Westlake, Tarrytown, Barton Creek, or a Lake Austin waterfront property

dining.description: Private-chef dining and exclusive catered events at home

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized plan plus concierge medicine and executive screenings

transportation.description: Multiple luxury vehicles, a dedicated driver for events, private car service

entertainment.description: A private box at UT games, philanthropic galas, art collecting, international travel

domesticHelp.description: Full-time housekeeper, personal assistant, and a pool/grounds crew

luxuryExtras.description: First-class international travel, a Hill Country ranch, a boat on Lake Travis, angel investing

10M.lifestyle: A top-of-market estate in Westlake or Barton Creek, or a waterfront property on Lake Austin, with full-time domestic staff, a private chef several days a week, and a personal assistant. Dining is anywhere, travel is first class, and a boat lives on Lake Travis, alongside donor-level support for local institutions. Texas's zero income tax keeps the full budget intact — roughly $225k a year — in a city with a relaxed pace and standout food and music.
